chapters.title: Core MedTech: one connected working process
lines: The pharmacy foundation is the operational heart: patient, prescription, stock and handover records.
The wider platform brings case teams, providers, billing staff and clients into a shared workflow.
Follow work from an assigned case to invoice review, receipt records and reporting.
Actual implemented screens. Synthetic records. Pre-authenticated test sessions.
Owner accepted the synthetic pilot. Production approval is a separate step.

chapters.text: The pharmacy foundation starts with the patient, prescription and case context. These are synthetic records.
This seeded ordinary fill retains pharmacist review, preparation and handover evidence. No medicine was dispensed.
The ordinary stock record retains the receipt and quantity. This segment is separate from the billing example that follows.
Start with an assigned case. Teams can work from shared case context instead of disconnected handoffs.
Provider: prepare an invoice against the right case, save a draft, then send it to the billing team.
The draft now moves into internal billing review. This is not a live insurer submission.
Billing staff review the invoice and leave a note. Responsibility stays clear as work changes hands.
Record a payment received elsewhere. MedTech keeps the evidence; it does not collect or move money.
Mistakes can be corrected with a reason. The original receipt remains in history.
Record a payment received elsewhere. MedTech keeps the evidence; it does not collect or move money.
The original entry, its reversal and the corrected receipt form a traceable record.
Client: see the relevant invoice and recorded balance. Other clients and unassigned case invoices stay out of view.
Settlement planning brings fees, costs and deductions together so the team can review a clear allocation.
An authorized administrator records completion. This changes a record; it does not transfer settlement funds.
Settlement corrections also retain the earlier record. The updated allocation stays explainable.
Reports turn the recorded work into a useful summary. Export a CSV for review and follow-up.
Private documents stay connected to the case. Authorized users can preview the original inside the workspace.
Manual EOB records support billing review today. No live payer feed is being shown.
A local appeal template gives staff a starting point. Human review is required; no AI or payer submission is connected.

chapters.title: The commercial opportunity
lines: One workflow connects legal, provider, billing and client work.
Clear handoffs can reduce follow-up friction and fragmented records.
Retained corrections make financial records easier to explain and review.
Shared documents and reports support a more organized service operation.

chapters.title: A substantial core is working. The next step is focused.
lines: The synthetic pilot is accepted and the core journeys run in a restored environment.
Next: owner feedback, remaining dependency findings and final release review.
Then: approved hosting, real backup/recovery checks, identity/mail and support readiness.
Any live provider connections need their own configuration and acceptance.

chapters.title: Ready for a core MedTech demonstration
lines: This is working software demonstrated with synthetic records.
The value is in connecting a complex, multi-role process with traceable history.
Production readiness remains a separate decision; no launch date is promised.
Owner review copy. No public live link or partner access has been created.
